newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Protestors, police clash before Amsterdam summit.
newsitem.headline: Protestors, police clash before Amsterdam summit.

text.p: Protesters clashed with police on Saturday when a street protest against hardship wrought by Europe's quest for monetary union turned violent.

Eye-witnesses told Reuters that as many as 150 demonstrators went on the rampage, smashing windows, overturning a police vehicle and pelting riot police with stones in Amsterdam's city centre district.
They said some demonstrators tried unsuccessfully to storm the Dutch central bank, which is hosting the summit of European Union leaders on Monday and Tuesday.
During the violence, which lasted about 45 minutes, fireworks were set off, bystanders were attacked and police made a handful of arrests.

"They're smashing the windows of the ABN AMRO bank. Police and marchers are scuffling. A couple of people have been arrested. There's also ambulances on the scene," Reuters photographer Jasper Juinen said.

Organisers of the European Marches Against Unemployment, Poverty and Social Exclusion said about 35,000 protesters earlier jammed the city's Dam square and walked through the streets to send a message to European leaders due here on Monday.
